title: Sound and finesse: Benny Carter, Don Byas, Coltrane and Sonny Rollins
summary: He prefers warm sound and finesse, thinks Coltrane sounds like a beginner beside Don Byas, and comments on Sonny Rollins, who studied writing with him along with Max Roach.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: But, see, I went more for the Benny Carter type of playing because Benny had the -- I always like the sound, I like a certain sound. Although, right now I still -- I listen to Don Byas and I hear a lot of Bird's passages now that Don plays. But he had the sound that was such a warm musical sound that it makes it -- I have a lot of records by Coltrane and I listen to Coltrane. He sounded like a beginner when you listen to Don Byas afterwards, although he was great. Great saxophone player but none of them go for finesse or sound.
Well, would you say Sonny Rollins has more of a sound?

Well, Sonny is unpredictible. He plays all kinds of things. He can play with sound, he plays some things that I wonder if he's going crazy, or what. And he studied with me for a while. But he and Max Roach both studied writing with me. And Sonny wanted to learn the clarinet but he gave it up.

But Sonny is a very fine saxophone player. But sometimes -- did you ever hear the album he did with Hawk? I couldn't imagine what he was thinking about to do what he did with Hawk, you know. Although I've heard him play great. I've heard him outstanding.
